newsitem.title: CANADA: There's life in the old horse yet-Morrison.
newsitem.headline: There's life in the old horse yet-Morrison.

text.p: Morrison Petroleums Ltd's deep natural gas well at Racehorse Creek has become a hot topic in Canada's oil patch since Canadian 88 Energy Corp launched a hostile bid for Morrison this month.

The much-watched well is amid large tracts of Morrison acreage in the southwestern Alberta foothills near the Crow's Nest Pass, a region known for deep and complex drilling and potentially rich gas reserves.

Racehorse Creek, which had been touted a "company-maker" exploration play for Morrison, failed to win, place or show in November after the company said it had drilling problems that forced operations to stop without a solid test.
What followed was a selloff in Morrison stock, which ultimately opened the door to Canadian 88's C$652 million offer for Morrison.

Canadian 88 covets Morrison's 153,000 acres in the region, which is estimated to carry a geological potential of 1.5 trillion cubic feet of gas. The foothills acreage surrounds Canadian 88 lands where the suitor made its own discovery at nearby Waterton with much fanfare last year.

On Friday, Canadian 88 chief executive Greg Noval criticized Morrison's financial and operating reporting for 1996, which, he said, booked 150 billion cubic feet of reserves in the foothills area, despite the lack of drilling success so far.
"Racehorse is a dead horse," Noval said.
But Morrison staff still believe they are running neck and neck with their next big discovery.
Morrison's problems in November were described as a chemical reaction that occurred when drilling mud mixed with acid used to test the reservoir, basically creating gypsum.
"We drywalled the inside of the hole, unfortunately," said Morrison senior geologist Paul McKay.
But the company moved the deep rig to an offsetting location and described as encouging results from current testing.

"It's very much an alive horse," MacKay said. "It can kick at us pretty good and we're confident it will kick again," he said.
